property_summary: For any address a, calling setOwner(a) as the current owner sets owner to exactly a; the mutant instead sets owner to msg.sender, so for a != msg.sender the assertion c.owner() == a fails.
For any address newOwner, a call to setOwner(newOwner) by the current owner makes c.owner() equal newOwner; the mutant never changes owner, so for newOwner != owner this rule is violated.

For any caller and any new owner, whenever a call to setOwner succeeds the contract's owner afterwards equals the requested new owner (and only the current owner's call succeeds); the mutant returns success without changing owner, so for a call from the current owner with a different new owner it succeeds while owner stays stale.

After transferring ownership to newOwner, that new owner can in turn call setOwner(other) and the owner becomes other; the mutant keeps the original owner, so the second call reverts and owner never equals other.
For any caller who is the current owner and any nonzero address a, calling setOwner(a) must leave owner() == a; the mutant instead always stores address(0), so it fails for any nonzero fuzzed a.
For any address a, calling setOwner(a) from the current owner must set owner to a; the mutant returns before the assignment, leaving owner unchanged, so for some a the invariant owner==a breaks.

For any caller and any new owner, calling setOwner changes owner to the new address exactly when the caller is the current owner (and leaves it unchanged otherwise); the mutant inverts the require so the owner's own call reverts and owner never changes, breaking the rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): non-owner's setOwner must revert and leave owner unchanged

property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner, setOwner(a) must make c.owner() exactly equal to a; the mutant instead rewrites owner to msg.sender, so for any proposed new owner different from the caller the invariant c.owner() == requestedOwner breaks.

When the current owner calls setOwner(a), the owner becomes exactly a, regardless of who the caller is; the mutant instead sets owner to msg.sender, so any requested owner different from the caller breaks c.owner() == requested.

Whenever the current owner calls setOwner(a), the owner must become exactly a (for any fuzzed a); the mutant overwrites owner with the caller instead, so for any a different from the caller the rule c.owner() == a is violated.

Whenever the CURRENT owner calls setOwner(a), ownership must become exactly a for every fuzzed a; the mutant instead rewrites owner to the caller during the modifier, so any requested owner differing from the caller breaks the rule — the key fix over prior attempts is driving the call from the actual owner (address(this), the deployer) rather than a fuzzed actor that is almost never the owner.

Ownership transferability: after the current owner delegates ownership to any fuzzed actor, that actor can set the owner to any fuzzed target, so c.owner() ends up exactly the requested target; the mutant rewrites owner to the caller in the modifier, so the delegated actor is not owner and its setOwner reverts, leaving owner != target.
For any caller that is the owner, a successful setOwner call returns true; the mutant returns false, breaking this rule for every (admissible) owner change input.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): successful setOwner must return true

property_summary: For any new owner address, a successful owner-only call to setOwner returns true; the mutant deletes the return so it returns false, breaking the rule.
For any caller that is not the current owner, setOwner must revert and never change owner; the mutant deletes the onlyOwner require, so a non-owner caller can change c.owner().
For every caller other than the current owner, c.setOwner must revert and leave c.owner() unchanged; the mutant lets any caller succeed, so it fails for some non-owner input the fuzzer finds.
For any admissible new owner address, a successful setOwner by the current owner must update the owner to that address and return true; the mutant always returns false and never updates the owner.

For every admissible input, after the current owner calls setOwner(_owner), c.owner() must equal _owner exactly as passed; the buggy version reverts when _owner is the zero address, leaving owner unchanged and thus violating the rule for that input.
For any address _owner, a call to setOwner(_owner) by the current owner succeeds and sets owner to _owner; the mutant reverts when _owner is the zero address, so the call does not succeed there.

For any admissible candidate address, a call to setOwner by the current owner must succeed and assign owner to that exact address; the mutant reverts when the address is zero, breaking the rule for that input.
